tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local linearization replay extending the prior ordered-turnover control. Initial authority is B={F_new,T_new}, effect E is uncommitted, and B issues one modeled atomic conditional primitive that commits E iff current authority identity equals expected {F_new,T_new} and E is uncommitted, with claim check, effect write and idempotency-marker write indivisible. Concurrently, authority turns over atomically from B to distinct non-reusable C={F_C,T_C}. The replay enumerates the only two legal total orders between B's first primitive and the turnover, then applies a stale B retry after turnover. No public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, external coordinator, richer-mode arbitration, or optional second semantic leaf was used.

fixture.atomic_effect_primitive: commit E iff current claim identity == expected {fence,token} AND E is uncommitted; authority predicate evaluation, effect write and idempotency marker write are one indivisible operation
fixture.race_assumption: the effect primitive and B-to-C authority turnover are linearizable with respect to the authority identity
case_effect_linearizes_before_turnover: 1. B's first primitive observes authority B and E uncommitted, so it atomically commits E and its idempotency marker.
2. Authority then turns over to C={F_C,T_C}.
3. B retries after an unknown acknowledgement outcome using stale expected {F_new,T_new}; current authority is C, so the retry is rejected and E remains committed exactly once.
case_turnover_linearizes_before_effect: 1. Authority first turns over from B to C={F_C,T_C}.
2. B's first primitive then observes nonmatching authority and performs no effect mutation.
3. B's later stale retry also observes C and performs no effect mutation.

required_assumptions: claim identity comparison, effect mutation and idempotency-marker mutation are atomic together
B-to-C authority turnover is linearizable relative to the effect primitive
C uses a distinct non-reusable fence+token
the effect-committed marker is durable across acknowledgement loss and turnover

observations: If B's effect primitive linearizes first, E is committed once before turnover and the post-turnover stale retry is rejected.
If turnover linearizes first, B's first primitive and stale retry are both rejected and E remains uncommitted.
Under the modeled linearizability assumptions there is no legal race ordering in which stale B can create a second E.
inference: Within this exact abstract replay and stated assumptions, a non-reusable authority identity plus an atomic conditional effect/idempotency primitive is at-most-once safe even when the first B effect attempt races authority turnover, because the two legal linearization orders yield effect counts 1 and 0 respectively and stale B is rejected after turnover. This does not prove exactly-once progress, single-winner acquisition/turnover, fork exclusion or liveness under real contention, nor that a concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed repository/API transport exposes the required atomic primitive.
unresolved_children: A concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent transport exposing a durable atomic conditional mutation over expected non-reusable fence+token, effect-uncommitted state and idempotency marker remains unverified.
Atomic single-winner claim acquisition and turnover keyed by stable effect identity remain unverified on a concrete allowed transport.
Fork exclusion and liveness under real contention remain unverified.
Exactly-once progress after the turnover-before-effect branch requires a current claimant retry/repair mechanism and remains unverified.
